\textbf{Analysis.} Between the three rounds of one configuration the frame time varies by 0.3--10.1\,ms, so differences of a few milliseconds are not significant. The night configuration (searchlights, beams, lamps, intruders, both \ab{622}{UAV} cameras rendering) costs +3.4\,ms over day (11.9 to 15.3\,ms). The thermal view frame is 1.0\,ms longer and draws 1.5\,M triangles against 4.1\,M in the visible view. Turning shadows off changes the day frame by +3.5\,ms, within that variation. Non-indexed drawing is the one large effect: +41.1\,ms (18.9\,\ab{623}{fps}), with non-indexed meshes every triangle stores its own three vertices instead of sharing them (a sphere: 3672 vertices instead of 614, Table~\ref{tab:prims}). Quality presets: LOW 12.6\,ms, HIGH 14.9\,ms, ULTRA 16.7\,ms, EPIC 11.9\,ms (ULTRA uses 8$\times$ \ab{624}{MSAA}, EPIC 4$\times$ plus \ab{625}{TAA}). In this headless setup much of a frame is \ab{626}{CPU} time: 4.4\,ms simulation and \ab{627}{UAV} camera submission plus 7.5\,ms rendering, of which 2.9\,ms is the \ab{628}{UAV} images' sensor model and \ab{629}{CV} (synchronous in the benchmark; on a worker thread in the game). Fastest: classic look (no post) day at 86\,\ab{630}{fps}.
